On October 28, my family and I decided to visit the Green Coffee Ecoland branch at around 9:30 pm. My wife, our three kids, and I were looking forward to enjoying a relaxing evening with some coffee. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be far from what we expected, largely due to a disturbing cleaning practice by the staff. At around 11:30 pm, the staff began cleaning the shop using what seemed to be a high concentration of Zonrox. Almost immediately, we were hit with a powerful, harsh odor that left us feeling uncomfortable and short of breath. I felt like I was almost suffocating from the fumes, and the smell lingered well after we left the coffee shop. Even two hours later, both my wife and I were still experiencing the effects of the fumes, which included lightheadedness and respiratory irritation. It’s alarming that such a strong cleaning product was used indoors while customers were still present. Zonrox, which contains bleach, can be highly irritating if inhaled and potentially harmful, especially in enclosed spaces without adequate ventilation. The fumes can cause symptoms like coughing, sore throat, and even headaches or nausea if exposure is prolonged. For children, this could be particularly risky. Additionally, the floors became slippery from the cleaning, making it quite unsafe. At one point, I nearly slipped on the wet floor—a dangerous situation that could have resulted in injury. It was disappointing to have to leave before closing time because the smell and unsafe conditions were too overwhelming to stay any longer. To the management at Green Coffee Ecoland, I would strongly recommend reassessing the timing and methods of cleaning practices. Using such harsh chemicals while customers are present is not only uncomfortable but poses potential health risks. I hope this feedback helps improve future experiences for other patrons and that appropriate adjustments are made to ensure safety and comfort in the shop.
